title: Mapping funds to goals, and step-up SIPs
objectives: Give each goal its own SIP and label, without multiplying funds.
Explain how a step-up SIP makes a large goal affordable.
body_md:
Give each goal its own SIP(s) and, where possible, its own folio or tag in the client's report, so progress is visible goal by goal. Avoid fund overlap across goals: the same 3–5 well-chosen funds can serve several long-term goals; label the units, don't multiply the funds. Put lump sums meant for distant goals into a liquid fund and move them in through an STP if the client is nervous about timing. Step-up SIPs: increase each SIP every year with income (for example 10%). In the education example, a 10% step-up cut the starting SIP from about ₹13,300 to about ₹7,700 for the same target.

> **Investor takeaway:** Label the units, don't multiply the funds.
example: Folio tag “Riya's college”: labelled money is less likely to be raided for a phone upgrade than an unlabelled balance — mental accounting, used well.
